question: Create a cited stormwater register for the Aurora facility’s final permit. Which outfall carries chemical monitoring, what does When Discharging require, and which published numbers are benchmarks rather than effluent limits?

question: Does representative chemistry at 001 excuse every 002 sample, and does annual report retention excuse submitting corrective reports? Build the qualified inspection/report register for this final source.
answer: No. The 002 Part I note exempts additional chemistry but expressly retains Flow Rate. Routine inspections are at least quarterly and at least once each calendar year during stormwater discharge; document them onsite with SWPPP unless agency submission is requested. The quarterly visual assessment provision names both 001 and 002; documented substantially identical-outfall determinations may permit rotating assessment across all represented outfalls, rather than indiscriminate omission. Benchmark first-eight-quarter/four-selected-quarter sampling differs from quarterly visual assessment. Annual reports are retained with SWPPP and need not be submitted unless requested. The specific corrective-action report must instead be submitted within 30 days of a triggering discovery, state completed or expected completion dates, and also be retained/included in annual reporting. These are source obligations, not evidence that the site performed inspections, qualifies for an inactive/E3 exception, submitted reports or repaired controls.

evidence.quote: 7. Benchmark Monitoring This permit stipulates pollutant benchmark concentrations that are applicable to certain sectors and subsectors and must be monitored within the first 2-years. The benchmark concentrations are not effluent limitations; a benchmark exceedance, therefore, is not a permit violation. Benchmark monitoring data are for your use to determine the overall effectiveness of your control measures and to assist you in knowing when additional corrective action(s) may be necessary to comply with the control measures/best management practices (BMPs) in Part IV. Items A-C. At your discretion, more than four samples may be taken during separate runoff events and used to determine the average benchmark parameter concentration for facility discharges. a. Benchmark Monitoring Schedule: During the first 8 quarterly monitoring periods of your permit coverage, you shall select a total of 4 quarterly monitoring periods and perform benchmark monitoring. Over this 2-year period, one benchmark sampling event shall be taken during each of the quarterly monitoring periods unless your facility is always inactive and unstaffed for a particular quarterly monitoring period. After collection of quarterly samples, you shall average your 4 monitoring values and compare to the benchmark concentration. b. Data Not Exceeding Benchmarks: After collection of 4 quarterly samples if the average of the 4 monitoring values for any parameter does not exceed the benchmark, you have fulfilled your monitoring requirements for that parameter for the permit term.
